source.text: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אַחַ֣ר׀שַׁלַּ֣ח אֹת֗וֹ נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֛ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֖ים מִן־הָֽרָמָ֑ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֹת֗וֹ וְהֽוּא־אָס֤וּר בָּֽאזִקִּים֙ בְּת֨וֹךְ כָּל־גָּל֤וּת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה הַמֻּגְלִ֖ים בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: The word that came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh after released him Nebuzaradan [the] chief of [the] guard from Ramah, when he took him, and he [was] bound in chains in [the] midst of all [the] exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who [were] being exiled to Babylon.

en.L: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, after Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard had released him from Ramah, when he took him, and he [was] bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had set him free at Ramah. Nebuzaradan had found him there bound in chains, among all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile in Babylon.
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan, the commander of the royal guard, set him free at Ramah. Jeremiah had been brought there in chains along with all the captives from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken away to Babylon.

es.L: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, después que Nabuzaradán, jefe de la guardia, lo dejó libre en Ramá, cuando lo tomó, estando él atado con cadenas en medio de todos los cautivos de Jerusalén y de Judá que eran llevados al destierro a Babilonia.
es.B: Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} después de que Nabuzaradán, capitán de la guardia, lo dejó en libertad en Ramá. Nabuzaradán lo había encontrado allí atado con cadenas, entre todos los cautivos de Jerusalén y de Judá que eran llevados al destierro en Babilonia.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Jeremías después de que Nabuzaradán, el comandante de la guardia real, lo dejó libre en Ramá. Habían llevado allí a Jeremías encadenado, junto con todos los cautivos de Jerusalén y de Judá que eran llevados a Babilonia.

sw.L: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, baada ya Nebuzaradani mkuu wa walinzi kumwachilia kutoka Rama, alipomchukua, naye [alikuwa] amefungwa kwa minyororo katikati ya mateka wote wa Yerusalemu na Yuda waliokuwa wakihamishwa kwenda Babeli.
sw.B: Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} baada ya Nebuzaradani kamanda wa walinzi kumwachilia huru huko Rama. Nebuzaradani alikuwa amemkuta huko amefungwa kwa minyororo, kati ya mateka wote wa Yerusalemu na Yuda waliokuwa wakichukuliwa uhamishoni Babeli.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Yeremia baada ya Nebuzaradani, kamanda wa walinzi wa mfalme, kumwachilia huru huko Rama. Yeremia alikuwa ameletwa huko akiwa amefungwa minyororo pamoja na mateka wote wa Yerusalemu na Yuda waliokuwa wakipelekwa Babeli.

decisions.choice: the heading stands over the account that follows; no message from the LORD is given until 42:7
alternatives: the heading introduces the captain's words in verses 2-3
the heading introduces a message given later, in 42:7
decisions.reason: This is the heading Jeremiah uses before a message from the LORD (7:1; 21:1), but here no message follows. The captain speaks in verses 2-5 and the story runs on, and the next word from the LORD comes in 42:7. The heading may introduce the whole account of chapters 40-44, which ends with the LORD's words through Jeremiah in Egypt. Or it may point to the captain's words in verses 2-3, which repeat what the LORD had said through Jeremiah. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: Ramah: a town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem, where the captives were gathered
decisions.reason: Ramah lay on the road north from Jerusalem. The Babylonians seem to have assembled the captives there before the long march to Babylon. It is the Ramah where Rachel is heard weeping for her children who are gone (31:15).

decisions.choice: a second account of Jeremiah's release, beside 39:11-14
decisions.reason: In 39:11-14 Nebuchadrezzar orders Jeremiah to be looked after, and the Babylonian officers take him from the courtyard of the guard and entrust him to Gedaliah. Here he is found in chains among the captives at Ramah. He may have been set free in Jerusalem and then swept up with the other captives, or the two passages may tell the same release from two different reports. Either way, both say he was freed by the Babylonians and went to Gedaliah.

decisions.choice: the chief of the guard: the commander of the king's bodyguard
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:8. The title is literally "chief of the slaughterers" or "of the cooks", an old court title for the officer in charge of the royal guard (Genesis 37:36; Jeremiah 39:9).

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L), with no "saying" and no colon; This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Here the Hebrew has no "saying" and no message follows directly, so Literal leaves out "saying", and no level ends the heading with a colon. Balanced and Readable put the rest of the verse in a second sentence.

decisions.choice: chief of the guard (Literal); captain of the guard (Balanced); commander of the royal guard (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:8. Balanced names Nebuzaradan again in its second sentence to make clear who found Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte del SEÑOR (L), without "diciendo" or a colon; Este mensaje vino ... (B); Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a Jeremías (R)
decisions.reason: The heading formula set for Jeremiah. The message itself does not follow at once; the story of Jeremiah's release comes first.

decisions.choice: jefe de la guardia (L); capitán de la guardia (B); comandante de la guardia real (R)
decisions.reason: The title as published 2 Kings 25:8.

decisions.choice: the heading formula without "kusema" and without a colon
decisions.reason: As the English: the heading stands over the account that follows, and no message is quoted after it.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֥ח רַב־טַבָּחִ֖ים לְיִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ דִּבֶּר֙ אֶת־הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took [the] chief of [the] guard Jeremiah, and he said to him, Yahweh your God spoke this disaster against this place.

en.L: And the chief of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God spoke this disaster against this place.
en.B: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God announced this disaster against this place.
en.R: The commander of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring this disaster on this place.

es.L: Y el jefe de la guardia tomó a Jeremías y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios habló este mal contra este lugar.
es.B: El capitán de la guardia llamó aparte a Jeremías y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios anunció esta calamidad contra este lugar.
es.R: El comandante de la guardia llamó aparte a Jeremías y le dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios dijo que traería esta desgracia sobre este lugar.

sw.L: Naye mkuu wa walinzi akamchukua Yeremia, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako aliyasema mabaya haya juu ya mahali hapa.
sw.B: Kamanda wa walinzi akamchukua Yeremia kando, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako aliyatangaza maafa haya juu ya mahali hapa.
sw.R: Kamanda wa walinzi akamchukua Yeremia kando, akamwambia, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alisema kwamba ataleta maafa haya juu ya mahali hapa.

decisions.choice: a Babylonian officer repeats the prophet's message
decisions.reason: The captain speaks of the LORD as Jeremiah's God and says what Jeremiah had said for forty years: the disaster came from the LORD because of Judah's sin. He may have heard Jeremiah's message from deserters or informers (38:19; 39:9), and he may only be using it to explain events. Either way, a foreign officer now confirms the word that Judah's own kings and leaders had refused.

decisions.choice: spoke this disaster: declared that this disaster would come
decisions.reason: To "speak a disaster" against a place is to announce it as a coming judgment (11:17; 19:15; 35:17; 36:31).

decisions.choice: this place: Jerusalem and the land of Judah
decisions.reason: As often in Jeremiah (7:3; 19:3), "this place" is the city and the land around it.

decisions.choice: took Jeremiah aside (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that he "took" Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable add "aside" to show that he singled Jeremiah out from the captives in order to speak to him.

decisions.choice: said he would bring this disaster on this place (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what it means to "speak" a disaster (m2).

source.text: וַיָּבֵ֥א וַיַּ֛עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־חֲטָאתֶ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ וְלֹֽא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם בְּקוֹל֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brought [it] and did Yahweh just as he spoke, for you sinned against Yahweh and did not listen to his voice, and has come to you the thing this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought [it] and has done just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke, because you sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, and this thing has happened to you.
en.B: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought it about and has done just what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, because you sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice. That is why this has happened to you.
en.R: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made it happen. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done just what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do. All this has happened to you people because you sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [lo] ha traído y ha hecho tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} habló, porque {{plural_you:ustedes pecaron|vosotros pecasteis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y no {{plural_you:escucharon|escuchasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz, y {{plural_you:les|os}} ha venido esto.
es.B: Ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha cumplido y ha hecho tal como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo, porque {{plural_you:pecaron|pecasteis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y no {{plural_you:obedecieron|obedecisteis}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voz. Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} ha sucedido esto.
es.R: Ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ha hecho realidad. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hecho tal como dijo que haría. Todo esto {{plural_you:les|os}} ha pasado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, la gente de este pueblo, porque {{plural_you:pecaron|pecasteis}} contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:obedecieron|obedecisteis}}.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameyaleta, akatenda kama alivyosema, kwa sababu mlimtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi, wala hamkuisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na jambo hili limewapata.
sw.B: Sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameyatimiza, amefanya sawasawa na alivyosema, kwa sababu mlimtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi wala hamkuitii sauti {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Ndiyo sababu jambo hili limewapata.
sw.R: Sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameyafanya yatokee. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amefanya sawasawa na alivyosema atafanya. Haya yote yamewapata ninyi watu kwa sababu mlimtenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} dhambi wala hamkumtii.

decisions.choice: "you" is plural: the people of Judah, not Jeremiah alone
decisions.reason: The captain speaks to Jeremiah, but the verbs and pronouns are plural. He is speaking of Judah as a whole, with Jeremiah as one of its people. He does not accuse Jeremiah himself, who had warned them.

decisions.choice: the captain echoes Jeremiah's own words
decisions.reason: "Because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey his voice ... this disaster has happened to you" is how Jeremiah himself explains the fall of Judah (32:23; 44:23). The captain's words sound like a summary of the prophet's message.

decisions.choice: listen to his voice: obey him
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone means to do what they say (7:23; 11:4).

decisions.choice: the thing with "the", as the margin reads
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "thing" without the article; the scribes' marginal reading adds "the" ("this thing"). The meaning is the same, and the marginal reading is followed.

decisions.choice: did not obey his voice (Balanced); did not obey him (Readable); you people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "obey" for the idiom (m3). Readable says "you people" to show that "you" is plural (m1) and puts the reason after the result.

decisions.choice: plural_you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural: Nebuzaradan speaks of Jeremiah's people as a whole, not of Jeremiah himself.

decisions.choice: "mlimtenda", "hamkuisikiliza", "limewapata" (plural "you")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural, the people of Judah, not Jeremiah alone; Swahili shows the plural in the verbs without adding a word.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה הִנֵּ֧ה פִתַּחְתִּ֣יךָ הַיּ֗וֹם מִֽן־הָאזִקִּים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־יָדֶךָ֒ אִם־ט֨וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֜יךָ לָב֧וֹא אִתִּ֣י בָבֶ֗ל בֹּ֚א וְאָשִׂ֤ים אֶת־עֵינִי֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וְאִם־רַ֧ע בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָבֽוֹא־אִתִּ֥י בָבֶ֖ל חֲדָ֑ל רְאֵה֙ כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶל־ט֨וֹב וְאֶל־הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָלֶ֥כֶת שָׁ֖מָּה לֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, here, I have released you today from the chains which [are] on your hand. If [it is] good in your eyes to come with me [to] Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you; and if [it is] bad in your eyes to come with me [to] Babylon, refrain. See, all the land [is] before you; to the good and to the right in your eyes to go, there go.

en.L: And now, look, I release you today from the chains that [are] on your hand. If it [is] good in your eyes to come with me [to] Babylon, come, and I will set my eye on you; but if it [is] bad in your eyes to come with me [to] Babylon, refrain. See, the whole land [is] before you; wherever [it is] good and right in your eyes to go, go there."
en.B: But now, today I am setting you free from the chains on your wrists. If you would like to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if you would rather not come with me to Babylon, then stay. See, the whole land lies open before you. Go wherever you think it good and right to go."
en.R: But today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free. If you want to come with me to Babylon, then come. I will take good care of you. But if you do not want to come with me to Babylon, you do not have to. Look, the whole country is open to you. Go wherever you think is best."

es.L: Y ahora, mira, yo te suelto hoy de las cadenas que [están] sobre tu mano. Si [es] bueno a tus ojos venir conmigo [a] Babilonia, ven, y yo pondré mis ojos sobre ti; pero si [es] malo a tus ojos venir conmigo [a] Babilonia, déjalo. Mira, toda la tierra [está] delante de ti; adonde [sea] bueno y recto a tus ojos ir, ve allá».
es.B: Pero ahora, hoy te libro de las cadenas que tienes en las muñecas. Si quieres venir conmigo a Babilonia, ven, y yo cuidaré de ti. Pero si prefieres no venir conmigo a Babilonia, quédate. Mira, toda la tierra está abierta delante de ti. Ve adonde te parezca bueno y recto ir».
es.R: Pero hoy te quito las cadenas de las muñecas y te dejo libre. Si quieres venir conmigo a Babilonia, ven. Yo te cuidaré bien. Pero si no quieres venir conmigo a Babilonia, no tienes que hacerlo. Mira, todo el país está abierto para ti. Ve adonde te parezca mejor».

sw.L: Na sasa, tazama, ninakufungua leo minyororo iliyo mkononi mwako. Ikiwa ni vema machoni pako kuja pamoja nami [hata] Babeli, njoo, nami nitaliweka jicho langu juu yako; lakini ikiwa ni vibaya machoni pako kuja pamoja nami [hata] Babeli, acha. Tazama, nchi yote iko mbele yako; mahali popote palipo pema na pa haki machoni pako kwenda, nenda huko."
sw.B: Lakini sasa, leo ninakufungua minyororo iliyo mikononi mwako. Ukipenda kuja pamoja nami Babeli, njoo, nami nitakutunza. Lakini usipopenda kuja pamoja nami Babeli, basi kaa. Tazama, nchi yote iko wazi mbele yako. Nenda popote unapoona ni vema na haki kwenda."
sw.R: Lakini leo ninakuondolea minyororo mikononi mwako na kukuacha huru. Ukitaka kuja pamoja nami Babeli, basi njoo. Nitakutunza vizuri. Lakini usipotaka kuja pamoja nami Babeli, si lazima uje. Tazama, nchi yote iko wazi kwako. Nenda popote unapoona ni bora."

decisions.choice: I release you today: the release takes effect as he speaks
decisions.reason: The verb has the form of a completed act, used for a declaration that is done by being said. With "today" it means that Jeremiah is free from this moment.

decisions.choice: good in your eyes ... bad in your eyes: if you want ... if you do not want
decisions.reason: "Good in your eyes" means "what seems good to you", what you wish (26:14). "Bad in your eyes" is the opposite: if you would rather not.

decisions.choice: I will set my eye on you: I will look after you
decisions.reason: To set one's eye on someone is to watch over them for their good, as Nebuchadrezzar had ordered for Jeremiah in 39:12 and as the LORD promises the exiles in 24:6.

decisions.choice: the whole land is before you: you may live wherever you choose
decisions.reason: The same words give Lot a free choice of land in Genesis 13:9, and Abimelech uses them to Abraham in Genesis 20:15. The captain gives Jeremiah the freedom of the country.

decisions.choice: hand (Literal); wrists (Balanced, Readable); refrain (Literal); stay (Balanced); you do not have to (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "hand", singular; Balanced and Readable say where chains are worn. Its verb for "do not come" means "leave off" or "refrain", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here and opens again in verse 5
decisions.reason: The captain's speech goes on in verse 5, but verse 5 begins with a remark by the narrator. The quotation is closed here and opened again after that remark.

decisions.choice: "ni vema machoni pako", "nitaliweka jicho langu juu yako" (L); "Ukipenda", "nitakutunza" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew pictures of the eyes; Balanced and Readable say "if you want" and "I will look after you".

source.text: וְעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ לֹֽא־יָשׁ֗וּב וְשֻׁ֡בָה אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֣ה בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־שָׁפָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ הִפְקִ֨יד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְשֵׁ֤ב אִתּוֹ֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֔ם א֠וֹ אֶל־כָּל־הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָלֶ֖כֶת לֵ֑ךְ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֧וֹ רַב־טַבָּחִ֛ים אֲרֻחָ֥ה וּמַשְׂאֵ֖ת וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he still not would return, and return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom appointed [the] king of Babylon over [the] cities of Judah, and stay with him in [the] midst of the people, or to all the right in your eyes to go, go. And gave to him [the] chief of [the] guard an allowance and a gift, and he sent him away.

en.L: And [while] he [was] still not turning back, "So return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever [it is] right in your eyes to go." And the chief of the guard gave him an allowance of food and a gift, and let him go.
en.B: Before Jeremiah had turned to go, Nebuzaradan added, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, the man the king of Babylon has set over the towns of Judah, and live with him among the people. Or go anywhere else you think right." Then the captain of the guard gave him food for the journey and a gift, and let him go.
en.R: Before Jeremiah turned to leave, Nebuzaradan said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan. The king of Babylon has put him in charge of the towns of Judah. Live with him among the people there. Or go anywhere else you choose." Then the commander of the guard gave Jeremiah food and a gift and let him go.

es.L: Y como él todavía no se volvía, [le dijo]: «Vuelve, pues, a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, a quien el rey de Babilonia ha puesto sobre las ciudades de Judá, y quédate con él en medio del pueblo; o ve adonde [sea] recto a tus ojos ir». Y el jefe de la guardia le dio provisiones y un regalo, y lo despidió.
es.B: Antes de que Jeremías se diera la vuelta para irse, Nabuzaradán añadió: «Vuelve a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, el hombre que el rey de Babilonia ha puesto sobre las ciudades de Judá, y vive con él entre el pueblo. O ve a cualquier otro lugar que te parezca bien». Entonces el capitán de la guardia le dio provisiones para el camino y un regalo, y lo dejó ir.
es.R: Antes de que Jeremías se fuera, Nabuzaradán le dijo: «Vuelve a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán. El rey de Babilonia lo ha puesto a cargo de las ciudades de Judá. Vive con él entre la gente de allí. O ve a cualquier otro lugar que quieras». Luego el comandante de la guardia le dio a Jeremías alimentos y un regalo, y lo dejó ir.

sw.L: Na [alipokuwa] bado hajageuka kurudi, "Basi rudi kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu mwana wa Shafani, ambaye mfalme wa Babeli amemweka juu ya miji ya Yuda, ukae naye katikati ya watu; au uende popote palipo haki machoni pako kwenda." Naye mkuu wa walinzi akampa posho la chakula na zawadi, akamwacha aende.
sw.B: Kabla Yeremia hajageuka kwenda, Nebuzaradani akaongeza, "Rudi kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, ambaye mfalme wa Babeli amemweka juu ya miji ya Yuda, ukae naye kati ya watu. Au nenda mahali pengine popote unapoona ni haki." Kisha kamanda wa walinzi akampa chakula cha safari na zawadi, akamwacha aende.
sw.R: Kabla Yeremia hajageuka kuondoka, Nebuzaradani akasema, "Rudi kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani. Mfalme wa Babeli amemweka kuwa msimamizi wa miji ya Yuda. Kaa naye kati ya watu walioko huko. Au nenda mahali pengine popote unapotaka." Kisha kamanda wa walinzi akampa Yeremia chakula na zawadi, akamwacha aende.

decisions.choice: And while he had not yet turned back: before Jeremiah could answer or leave, the captain went on
alternatives: Jeremiah still hesitated to go back, so the captain urged him
a damaged text, read differently by the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this clause is obscure. Word for word it says "and he still would not return", followed at once by "and return to Gedaliah". It is read here as a remark that Jeremiah had not yet turned to go, or had not yet answered, when the captain added his advice. Others take it to mean that Jeremiah hesitated, so the captain urged him. The Greek translation seems to have read a different text here, something like "but if not, run back". The Hebrew is followed, and the reading is uncertain. The account of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: Gedaliah: the governor appointed over Judah
decisions.reason: On Gedaliah and his family see 2 Kings 25:22. His father Ahikam had protected Jeremiah years before (26:24). The captain points Jeremiah to the man now in charge of the land.

decisions.choice: an allowance: a ration of food
decisions.reason: The word names a set portion of food, like the daily allowance given to King Jehoiachin in Babylon (52:34; 2 Kings 25:30). With the gift, it shows the care the captain had promised in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Nebuzaradan added (Balanced); Nebuzaradan said (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew goes straight into the captain's words without saying who speaks. Balanced and Readable name him, since the clause before is about Jeremiah. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew.

decisions.choice: food for the journey (Balanced); food (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the purpose of the allowance (m3); Readable keeps it simple.

decisions.choice: [le dijo]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins this verse without a word of speaking; Literal supplies one in brackets, where the English Literal opens the quotation without it.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֥ה בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֖ם הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב אִתּוֹ֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֔ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came Jeremiah to Gedaliah son of Ahikam [to] Mizpah, and he stayed with him in [the] midst of the people who remained in the land.

en.L: And Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.
en.B: So Jeremiah went to Mizpah, to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and lived there with him among the people left in the land.
en.R: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. He stayed there with him among the people who had been left behind in the land.

es.L: Y fue Jeremías a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, a Mizpa, y habitó con él en medio del pueblo que había quedado en la tierra.
es.B: Así que Jeremías fue a Mizpa, a ver a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, y vivió allí con él entre el pueblo que había quedado en la tierra.
es.R: Así que Jeremías fue a ver a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam en Mizpa. Se quedó allí con él entre la gente que había quedado en el país.

sw.L: Basi Yeremia akaenda kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu huko Mizpa, akakaa naye katikati ya watu waliobaki katika nchi.
sw.B: Basi Yeremia akaenda Mizpa kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, akakaa huko pamoja naye kati ya watu waliobaki katika nchi.
sw.R: Basi Yeremia akaenda kwa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu huko Mizpa. Akakaa huko pamoja naye kati ya watu waliokuwa wameachwa katika nchi.

decisions.choice: Mizpah: a town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:23. With Jerusalem in ruins, Gedaliah governed from Mizpah, a few miles to the north.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah chooses to stay in the land
decisions.reason: He could have gone to Babylon under the captain's protection. He stayed with the poor who were left. His choice fits his message that life would go on in the land: "houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land" (32:15).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֩ כָל־שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה הֵ֚מָּה וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־הִפְקִ֧יד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכִ֣י׀הִפְקִ֣יד אִתּ֗וֹ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים וְנָשִׁים֙ וָטָ֔ף וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־הָגְל֖וּ בָּבֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] in the field, they and their men, that had appointed [the] king of Babylon Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had entrusted to him men and women and little ones, and from [the] poor of the land, from those who had not been exiled to Babylon,

en.L: And all the commanders of the forces who [were] in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had entrusted to him men and women and little ones, and some of the poorest of the land, of those who had not been taken into exile to Babylon,
en.B: All the commanders of the forces who were in the open country and their men learned that the king of Babylon had set Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had placed in his care men, women and children, those of the poorest people of the land who had not been taken into exile to Babylon,
en.R: All the army commanders and their men who were still out in the open country heard that the king of Babylon had put Gedaliah son of Ahikam in charge of the land. They heard that he had also put Gedaliah in charge of the men, women and children who had not been taken away to Babylon, the poorest people in the land.

es.L: Y oyeron todos los jefes de las tropas que [estaban] en el campo, ellos y sus hombres, que el rey de Babilonia había puesto a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam sobre la tierra, y que le había encomendado hombres, mujeres y niños, y de los pobres de la tierra, de los que no habían sido llevados cautivos a Babilonia,
es.B: Todos los jefes de las tropas que estaban en el campo, y sus hombres, se enteraron de que el rey de Babilonia había nombrado a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam sobre la tierra y había puesto a su cargo a hombres, mujeres y niños, los más pobres del país que no habían sido llevados al destierro en Babilonia,
es.R: Todos los jefes del ejército y sus hombres, que todavía estaban en el campo, oyeron que el rey de Babilonia había puesto a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam a cargo del país. Oyeron que también lo había puesto a cargo de los hombres, las mujeres y los niños que no habían sido llevados a Babilonia, la gente más pobre del país.

sw.L: Nao wakuu wote wa majeshi waliokuwa nyikani, wao na watu wao, waliposikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli amemweka Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu juu ya nchi, na kwamba amemkabidhi wanaume na wanawake na watoto, na baadhi ya maskini wa nchi, wale ambao hawakuhamishwa kwenda Babeli,
sw.B: Wakuu wote wa majeshi waliokuwa nyikani pamoja na watu wao walisikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli amemweka Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu juu ya nchi, na kwamba amemkabidhi wanaume, wanawake na watoto, wale wa watu maskini kabisa wa nchi ambao hawakuchukuliwa uhamishoni Babeli,
sw.R: Makamanda wote wa jeshi na watu wao waliokuwa bado nyikani walisikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli amemweka Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu kuwa msimamizi wa nchi. Walisikia kwamba amemweka Gedalia pia kuwa msimamizi wa wanaume, wanawake na watoto ambao hawakupelekwa Babeli, watu maskini kabisa wa nchi.

decisions.choice: the account of 2 Kings 25:23-24, told more fully
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 tell what 2 Kings 25:23-24 tells, often in the same words. Jeremiah adds that the commanders were "in the open country", that Gedaliah was set "over the land", and that the people left behind were put in his care. Verses 10-16 have no parallel in Kings.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the forces in the open country: Judah's officers still at large
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:23. When the city fell, the army scattered (39:4-5; 52:7-8), and some officers stayed out in the countryside with their men.

decisions.choice: and some of the poorest: the men, women and children left were the poor of the land
decisions.reason: The "and" introduces who these people were rather than a second group. The Babylonians had taken the leading families into exile and left the poorest people to work the land (39:10; 52:16; 2 Kings 25:12).

decisions.choice: wording of 2 Kings 25:23 reused; the sentence runs on into verse 8
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew is the same as 2 Kings 25:23, Literal and Readable keep the wording used there, and Balanced stays close to it ("set ... over the land" for "appointed"). The sentence continues into verse 8, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma; Readable makes two sentences of it.

decisions.choice: wording of 2 Kings 25:23 reused (los jefes de las tropas, Mizpa, the list of names)
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 tell what 2 Kings 25:23-24 tells, more fully; the published Spanish is reused where the Hebrew is the same. The sentence runs on into verse 8.

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa majeshi" (L, B), "makamanda wa jeshi" (R), as 2 Kings 25:23
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 40:7-9 tells again 2 Kings 25:23-24; the Swahili wording of that passage is kept where the Hebrew is the same.

en.B: and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, together with their men.
en.R: So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai from the town of Netophah, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite. Their men came with them.

es.B: y fueron a ver a Gedalías en Mizpa. Eran Ismael hijo de Netanías, Johanán y Jonatán hijos de Carea, Seraías hijo de Tanhumet, los hijos de Efai el netofatita y Jezanías hijo del maacateo, junto con sus hombres.
es.R: Así que fueron a ver a Gedalías en Mizpa. Eran Ismael hijo de Netanías, Johanán y Jonatán hijos de Carea, Seraías hijo de Tanhumet, los hijos de Efai, de la ciudad de Netofa, y Jezanías hijo del maacateo. Sus hombres fueron con ellos.

sw.R: Basi wakaja kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa. Hao walikuwa Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania, Yohana na Yonathani wana wa Karea, Seraya mwana wa Tanhumethi, wana wa Efai kutoka mji wa Netofa, na Yezania mwana wa Mmaakathi. Watu wao walikuja pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: a fuller list than 2 Kings 25:23
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:23 names Ishmael, Johanan, Seraiah and Jaazaniah. Jeremiah adds Jonathan, Johanan's brother, and the sons of Ephai. In Kings "the Netophathite" belongs to Seraiah; here it belongs to the sons of Ephai. Jezaniah is another spelling of the name Jaazaniah.

decisions.choice: Ephai, as the margin reads
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a name that would be read Ophai; the scribes' marginal reading is Ephai, which is followed. Either way it is the same man.

decisions.choice: the Netophathite; the Maacathite
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:23: Netophah was a town near Bethlehem, and the Maacathites were a clan named for Maacah, a small Aramean region northeast of Galilee.

decisions.choice: Ishmael and Johanan: the two men the next chapters follow
decisions.reason: Ishmael will murder Gedaliah (41:1-3), and Johanan will lead the survivors who go down to Egypt (41:11-43:7).

decisions.choice: from the town of Netophah (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:23.

decisions.choice: Jezanías
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here has the form Jezaniah; 2 Kings 25:23 has Jaazaniah for the same man. Each keeps its own form.

decisions.choice: "Yohana mwana wa Karea", as 2 Kings 25:23
decisions.reason: The published Swahili form; this Johanan is an army officer of Judah, not John the Baptist or the apostle, who share the Swahili name. "Yezania" keeps this verse's spelling, where 2 Kings 25:23 has "Yaazania".

source.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע לָהֶ֜ם גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֤ם בֶּן־שָׁפָן֙ וּלְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־תִּֽירְא֖וּ מֵעֲב֣וֹד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים שְׁב֣וּ בָאָ֗רֶץ וְעִבְד֛וּ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְיִיטַ֥ב לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And swore to them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan and to their men, saying, Do not fear to serve the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well for you.

en.L: And Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men, saying, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.
en.B: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, gave them and their men his sworn word. "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans," he said. "Settle in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and all will go well with you.
en.R: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, gave them and their men his promise, and he swore an oath to keep it. "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians," he said. "Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you.

es.L: Y Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, les juró a ellos y a sus hombres, diciendo: «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de servir a los caldeos; {{plural_you:habiten|habitad}} en la tierra y {{plural_you:sirvan|servid}} al rey de Babilonia, y {{plural_you:les|os}} irá bien.
es.B: Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, les dio su palabra con juramento a ellos y a sus hombres. «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de servir a los caldeos», les dijo. «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} a vivir en la tierra, {{plural_you:sirvan|servid}} al rey de Babilonia, y todo {{plural_you:les|os}} irá bien.
es.R: Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, les hizo una promesa a ellos y a sus hombres, y juró que la cumpliría. «No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de servir a los babilonios», les dijo. «{{plural_you:Quédense|Quedaos}} en el país y {{plural_you:sirvan|servid}} al rey de Babilonia. Así {{plural_you:les|os}} irá bien.

sw.L: Naye Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu mwana wa Shafani akawaapia wao na watu wao, kusema, "Msiogope kuwatumikia Wakaldayo. Kaeni katika nchi, mtumikieni mfalme wa Babeli, nanyi mtakuwa salama.
sw.B: Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, aliwaapia wao na watu wao. Akasema, "Msiogope kuwatumikia Wakaldayo. Kaeni katika nchi, mtumikieni mfalme wa Babeli, nanyi mtafanikiwa.
sw.R: Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, aliwapa wao na watu wao ahadi, akaapa kwamba ataitimiza. Akasema, "Msiogope kuwatumikia Wababeli. Kaeni katika nchi na kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli. Ndipo mambo yatawaendea vizuri.

decisions.choice: "to serve the Chaldeans", where 2 Kings 25:24 has "of the servants of the Chaldeans"
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew phrases differ by little more than a letter. In Kings the commanders are told not to fear the Babylonian officials; here they are told not to fear serving Babylon. Jeremiah also names Gedaliah's father and grandfather and adds "saying". The rest of the oath is word for word the same as Kings.

decisions.choice: swore to them: gave his word under oath
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:24. Gedaliah guaranteed with an oath that the commanders and their men would be safe if they accepted Babylonian rule.

decisions.choice: the counsel Jeremiah had given
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:24. Gedaliah repeats Jeremiah's message: serve the king of Babylon and live (27:11-12; 38:17), settle where you are and seek its good (29:4-7).

decisions.choice: Chaldeans (Literal, Balanced); Babylonians (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 25:24 is reused at Literal and Readable where the Hebrew is the same; Balanced says "gave them ... his sworn word" for "swore an oath to them", with the same sense. Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans", as everywhere in Jeremiah. The speech goes on in verse 10, so the quotation stays open.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י יֹשֵׁב֙ בַּמִּצְפָּ֔ה לַֽעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖אוּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וְאַתֶּ֡ם אִסְפוּ֩ יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן וְשִׂ֨מוּ֙ בִּכְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֵיכֶ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־תְּפַשְׂתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, here I [am] dwelling at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us; and you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put [them] in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have seized.

en.L: And as for me, look, I am staying at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us; but you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put [them] in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken."
en.B: As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you are to gather the wine, the summer fruit and the oil, store them in your jars, and live in the towns you have taken over."
en.R: I will stay here at Mizpah and speak for you to the Babylonians who come to us. But you must gather in the wine, the summer fruit and the olive oil, and store them in your jars. Then settle in the towns you have taken over."

es.L: Y en cuanto a mí, he aquí, yo habito en Mizpa para estar delante de los caldeos que vengan a nosotros; pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:recojan|recoged}} vino y fruta de verano y aceite, y {{plural_you:pónganlos|ponedlos}} en {{plural_you:sus vasijas|vuestras vasijas}}, y {{plural_you:habiten|habitad}} en {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}} que {{plural_you:han tomado|habéis tomado}}».
es.B: En cuanto a mí, me quedaré en Mizpa para {{plural_you:representarlos|representaros}} ante los caldeos que vengan a nosotros. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:recojan|recoged}} el vino, la fruta de verano y el aceite, {{plural_you:guárdenlos|guardadlos}} en {{plural_you:sus tinajas|vuestras tinajas}} y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} en las ciudades que {{plural_you:han ocupado|habéis ocupado}}».
es.R: Yo me quedaré aquí en Mizpa y hablaré a favor {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} ante los babilonios que vengan a nosotros. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:recojan|recoged}} la cosecha de uvas para el vino, la fruta de verano y el aceite de oliva, y {{plural_you:guárdenlos|guardadlos}} en {{plural_you:sus tinajas|vuestras tinajas}}. Luego {{plural_you:establézcanse|estableceos}} en las ciudades que {{plural_you:han ocupado|habéis ocupado}}».

sw.L: Nami, tazama, ninakaa Mizpa ili kusimama mbele ya Wakaldayo watakaokuja kwetu; lakini ninyi, kusanyeni divai na matunda ya kiangazi na mafuta, mkaviweke katika vyombo vyenu, mkae katika miji yenu mliyoitwaa."
sw.B: Kwa upande wangu, nitakaa Mizpa ili niwawakilishe mbele ya Wakaldayo watakaokuja kwetu. Lakini ninyi kusanyeni divai, matunda ya kiangazi na mafuta, mkaviweke katika mitungi yenu, mkae katika miji mliyoitwaa."
sw.R: Mimi nitakaa hapa Mizpa na kuwasemea mbele ya Wababeli watakaokuja kwetu. Lakini ninyi vuneni divai, matunda ya kiangazi na mafuta ya zeituni, mkaviweke katika mitungi yenu. Kisha mkae katika miji mliyoichukua."

decisions.choice: to stand before the Chaldeans: to answer to them on the people's behalf
decisions.reason: To "stand before" someone is to serve and attend on them, as an official stands before a king (52:12). Gedaliah will be the one who deals with the Babylonian officers, so that the people can get on with their lives.

decisions.choice: wine, summer fruit and oil: the late summer and autumn harvest
decisions.reason: The city fell in the fifth month, midsummer (52:12). Grapes, figs and other summer fruit, and olives were ripening in the following months, and the fields of those taken into exile had no one else to harvest them. "Wine" and "oil" here name the crops gathered to make them.

decisions.choice: your towns that you have taken over
decisions.reason: The verb means "seize" or "take hold of". The towns had been emptied by war and exile, and the commanders and their men had occupied them. Gedaliah tells them to settle there.

decisions.choice: jars (Balanced, Readable); olive oil, gather in (Readable)
decisions.reason: The "vessels" were storage jars. Readable says "olive oil" and "gather in" to make the harvest clear (m2).

source.text: וְגַ֣ם כָּֽל־הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר־בְּמוֹאָ֣ב׀וּבִבְנֵֽי־עַמּ֨וֹן וּבֶאֱד֜וֹם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּכָל־הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל שְׁאֵרִ֖ית לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וְכִי֙ הִפְקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֥ם בֶּן־שָׁפָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And also all the Judeans who [were] in Moab and among [the] sons of Ammon and in Edom, and who [were] in all the lands, heard that had given [the] king of Babylon a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan,

en.L: And also all the Judeans who [were] in Moab and among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon and in Edom, and who [were] in all the lands, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant to Judah, and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan,
en.B: Likewise, all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had allowed a remnant to stay in Judah, with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, set over them,
en.R: All the Judeans who were living in Moab, Ammon, Edom and the other countries heard about this. They heard that the king of Babylon had let some people stay in Judah, and that he had put Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, in charge of them.

es.L: Y también todos los judíos que [estaban] en Moab, y entre los hijos de Amón, y en Edom, y los que [estaban] en todas las tierras, oyeron que el rey de Babilonia había dejado un remanente en Judá, y que había puesto sobre ellos a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán,
es.B: Asimismo, todos los judíos que estaban en Moab, entre los amonitas, en Edom y en todas las demás tierras oyeron que el rey de Babilonia había dejado un remanente en Judá, y que había puesto sobre ellos a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán,
es.R: Todos los judíos que vivían en Moab, en Amón, en Edom y en los demás países se enteraron de esto. Oyeron que el rey de Babilonia había dejado que algunas personas se quedaran en Judá, y que había puesto a Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, a cargo de ellos.

sw.L: Tena Wayahudi wote waliokuwa Moabu, na kati ya wana wa Amoni, na Edomu, na waliokuwa katika nchi zote, waliposikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli amewaachia Yuda mabaki, na kwamba amemweka juu yao Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu mwana wa Shafani,
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, Wayahudi wote waliokuwa Moabu, kati ya Waamoni, Edomu na katika nchi nyingine zote walisikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli ameruhusu mabaki wabaki Yuda, na kwamba amemweka Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, juu yao,
sw.R: Wayahudi wote waliokuwa wakiishi Moabu, Amoni, Edomu na nchi nyingine walisikia habari hii. Walisikia kwamba mfalme wa Babeli amewaruhusu watu wachache wabaki Yuda, na kwamba amemweka Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, kuwa msimamizi wao.

decisions.choice: Judeans in Moab, Ammon and Edom: refugees from the invasions
decisions.reason: Moab, Ammon and Edom lay east and southeast of Judah, across the Jordan and the Dead Sea. People of Judah had fled there during the Babylonian invasions; verse 12 says they had been "driven" there.

decisions.choice: the Judeans: the people of the kingdom of Judah
decisions.reason: The word means people of Judah. The later word "Jew" comes from it, but here it names the people of the kingdom that had just fallen.

decisions.choice: had given a remnant to Judah: had allowed some of the people to remain
decisions.reason: The king of Babylon had not emptied the land completely. A remnant was left, and Gedaliah was set over them.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 12
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end with a comma, since the sentence continues. Readable makes two sentences and says "let some people stay" for "gave a remnant".

decisions.choice: un remanente (L, B); algunas personas (R)
decisions.reason: "Remnant" is "el remanente" at Literal and Balanced in this translation; Readable says who they were. "Hijos de Amón" already includes women, so no gender span.

decisions.choice: "mabaki" (L, B); "watu wachache" (R)
decisions.reason: The word set for the remnant: "mabaki" at Literal and Balanced, as Romans 9:27 and 2 Kings 19:31; Readable says it plainly. "wana wa Amoni" at Literal takes no gender span: "wana" already includes daughters.

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ כָל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים מִכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִדְּחוּ־שָׁ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ אֶֽרֶץ־יְהוּדָ֛ה אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וַיַּאַסְפ֛וּ יַ֥יִן וָקַ֖יִץ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and returned all the Judeans from all the places where they had been driven there, and they came [to the] land of Judah to Gedaliah [to] Mizpah, and they gathered wine and summer fruit very much exceedingly.

en.L: and all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven, and they came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they gathered wine and summer fruit in very great abundance.
en.B: and all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been scattered. They came back to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and brought in a very large harvest of wine and summer fruit.
en.R: So all these Judeans came back to the land of Judah from all the places where they had been scattered. They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. And they gathered a very large harvest of wine and summer fruit.

es.L: y volvieron todos los judíos de todos los lugares adonde habían sido arrojados, y vinieron a la tierra de Judá, a Gedalías, a Mizpa, y recogieron vino y fruta de verano en gran abundancia.
es.B: y todos los judíos regresaron de todos los lugares por donde habían sido dispersados. Volvieron a la tierra de Judá, a Gedalías en Mizpa, y recogieron una cosecha muy abundante de vino y fruta de verano.
es.R: Así que todos estos judíos regresaron a la tierra de Judá desde todos los lugares donde habían sido dispersados. Fueron a ver a Gedalías en Mizpa. Y recogieron una cosecha muy grande de uvas para el vino y de fruta de verano.

sw.L: Ndipo Wayahudi wote wakarudi kutoka mahali pote walipokuwa wamefukuzwa, wakaja katika nchi ya Yuda, kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa, wakakusanya divai na matunda ya kiangazi mengi sana.
sw.B: Wayahudi wote walirudi kutoka mahali pote walipokuwa wametawanyika. Wakarudi katika nchi ya Yuda, kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa, wakavuna divai na matunda ya kiangazi kwa wingi sana.
sw.R: Basi Wayahudi hao wote walirudi katika nchi ya Yuda kutoka mahali pote walipokuwa wametawanyika. Wakaja kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa. Wakavuna divai na matunda ya kiangazi kwa wingi sana.

decisions.choice: a small first return
decisions.reason: "The places where they had been driven" is the language Jeremiah uses for the LORD's promise to bring his people back (23:3, 8; 29:14; 32:37). For a short time the scattered people of Judah come home and the land gives its harvest. The next chapter shows how quickly this hope was broken.

decisions.choice: a very large harvest
decisions.reason: The harvest Gedaliah had told them to gather (verse 10) was plentiful. Oil is not named this time; the olives ripened last, later in the autumn.

decisions.choice: scattered (Balanced, Readable); a very large harvest (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be driven away or scattered. Balanced and Readable turn "they gathered wine and summer fruit very much" into "a very large harvest".

source.text: וְיֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה בָּ֥אוּ אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ הַמִּצְפָּֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] in the field came to Gedaliah [to] Mizpah,

en.L: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who [were] in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah,
en.B: Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
en.R: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were out in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.

es.L: Y Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes de las tropas que [estaban] en el campo vinieron a Gedalías, a Mizpa,
es.B: Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes de las tropas que estaban en el campo fueron a ver a Gedalías en Mizpa
es.R: Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes del ejército que todavía estaban en el campo fueron a ver a Gedalías en Mizpa.

sw.L: Naye Yohana mwana wa Karea na wakuu wote wa majeshi waliokuwa nyikani wakaja kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa,
sw.B: Yohana mwana wa Karea na wakuu wote wa majeshi waliokuwa nyikani walikuja kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa,
sw.R: Yohana mwana wa Karea na makamanda wote wa jeshi waliokuwa nyikani walikuja kwa Gedalia huko Mizpa.

decisions.choice: a new scene, some time later
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Johanan's name first, before the verb, which marks the start of a new episode. The commanders had already come to Gedaliah once (verse 8); this is a later visit.

decisions.choice: Johanan son of Kareah
decisions.reason: Johanan is named first among the commanders from here on. He will rescue the captives Ishmael takes (41:11-16) and then lead the people to Egypt (43:4-7).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 14
decisions.reason: Literal ends with a comma; Balanced runs straight on into verse 14 with no comma before "and said"; Readable makes a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו הֲיָדֹ֤עַתֵּדַע֙ כִּ֞י בַּעֲלִ֣יס׀מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֗וֹן שָׁלַח֙ אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֔ה לְהַכֹּתְךָ֖ נָ֑פֶשׁ וְלֹא־הֶאֱמִ֣ין לָהֶ֔ם גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and they said to him, Do you indeed know that Baalis king of [the] sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you [in] life? And did not believe them Gedaliah son of Ahikam.

en.L: and they said to him, "Do you indeed know that Baalis king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you dead?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.
en.B: and asked him, "Do you realize that Baalis, the Ammonite king, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to murder you?" Gedaliah son of Ahikam, however, would not believe them.
en.R: They asked him, "Do you know that Baalis, who is king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

es.L: y le dijeron: «¿Sabes de cierto que Baalis, rey de los hijos de Amón, ha enviado a Ismael hijo de Netanías para quitarte la vida?». Pero Gedalías hijo de Ahicam no les creyó.
es.B: y le preguntaron: «¿Te das cuenta de que Baalis, el rey amonita, ha enviado a Ismael hijo de Netanías para asesinarte?». Pero Gedalías hijo de Ahicam no quiso creerles.
es.R: Le preguntaron: «¿Sabes que Baalis, el rey de los amonitas, ha enviado a Ismael hijo de Netanías para matarte?». Pero Gedalías hijo de Ahicam no les creyó.

sw.L: wakamwambia, "Je, unajua kweli kwamba Baalisi mfalme wa wana wa Amoni amemtuma Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania akuue?" Lakini Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu hakuwasadiki.
sw.B: wakamwuliza, "Je, unajua kwamba Baalisi, mfalme wa Waamoni, amemtuma Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania akuue?" Hata hivyo, Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu hakuwaamini.
sw.R: Wakamwuliza, "Je, unajua kwamba Baalisi, mfalme wa Waamoni, amemtuma Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania akuue?" Lakini Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu hakuwaamini.

decisions.choice: Do you indeed know ...? an urgent warning
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: "knowing, do you know?" It is a pressing question that means "Surely you know" or "You must realize".

decisions.choice: Baalis king of Ammon
decisions.reason: Ammon lay east of the Jordan. Its king had once joined Judah in plotting against Babylon (27:3). Why he wanted Gedaliah dead is not said; a governor loyal to Babylon may have stood in his way. After the murder Ishmael fled to the Ammonites (41:10, 15).

decisions.choice: to strike you in life: to kill you
decisions.reason: "To strike someone in life" means to strike a fatal blow (Genesis 37:21; Deuteronomy 19:6, 11).

decisions.choice: strike you dead (Literal); murder you (Balanced); kill you (Readable); Do you realize (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a blow; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3). Balanced puts the doubled verb as "Do you realize" (m1).

source.text: וְיוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֡חַ אָמַ֣ר אֶל־גְּדַלְיָהוּ֩ בַסֵּ֨תֶר בַּמִּצְפָּ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר אֵ֤לְכָה נָּא֙ וְאַכֶּה֙ אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֔ה וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א יֵדָ֑ע לָ֧מָּה יַכֶּ֣כָּה נֶּ֗פֶשׁ וְנָפֹ֨צוּ֙ כָּל־יְהוּדָ֔ה הַנִּקְבָּצִ֣ים אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאָבְדָ֖ה שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Johanan son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah, saying, Let me go, please, and let me strike Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and a man will not know; why should he strike you [in] life, and be scattered all Judah who are gathered to you, and perish [the] remnant of Judah?

en.L: And Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah, saying, "Let me go, please, and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike you dead, and all Judah who are gathered to you be scattered, and the remnant of Judah perish?"
en.B: Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah privately at Mizpah. "Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah," he said, "and no one will know. Why should he take your life, so that all the Judeans gathered around you are scattered and the remnant of Judah perishes?"
en.R: Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in private at Mizpah. "Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah," he said. "Nobody will find out who did it. Why should he kill you? Then all the people of Judah who have gathered around you would be scattered, and the few people left in Judah would be wiped out."

es.L: Y Johanán hijo de Carea habló a Gedalías en secreto en Mizpa, diciendo: «Déjame ir, por favor, y mataré a Ismael hijo de Netanías, y nadie lo sabrá. ¿Por qué ha de quitarte la vida, y se dispersen todos los de Judá que se han reunido en torno a ti, y perezca el remanente de Judá?».
es.B: Entonces Johanán hijo de Carea le habló a Gedalías en privado en Mizpa. «Por favor, déjame ir a matar a Ismael hijo de Netanías», le dijo, «y nadie lo sabrá. ¿Por qué ha de quitarte la vida, para que se dispersen todos los judíos reunidos en torno a ti y perezca el remanente de Judá?».
es.R: Luego Johanán hijo de Carea le habló a Gedalías en privado en Mizpa. «Por favor, déjame ir a matar a Ismael hijo de Netanías», le dijo. «Nadie sabrá quién lo hizo. ¿Por qué ha de matarte él? Si lo hace, toda la gente de Judá que se ha reunido en torno a ti se dispersará, y los pocos que quedan en Judá serán destruidos».

sw.L: Naye Yohana mwana wa Karea akasema na Gedalia kwa siri huko Mizpa, kusema, "Tafadhali niache niende nikampige Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania, wala hakuna mtu atakayejua. Kwa nini akuue, na Wayahudi wote waliokusanyika kwako watawanyike, na mabaki ya Yuda yaangamie?"
sw.B: Kisha Yohana mwana wa Karea akazungumza na Gedalia faraghani huko Mizpa. Akasema, "Tafadhali niruhusu niende nikamuue Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania, wala hakuna mtu atakayejua. Kwa nini akuue, hata Wayahudi wote waliokusanyika kwako watawanyike, na mabaki ya Yuda yaangamie?"
sw.R: Kisha Yohana mwana wa Karea akazungumza na Gedalia kwa siri huko Mizpa. Akasema, "Tafadhali niruhusu niende nikamuue Ishmaeli mwana wa Nethania. Hakuna mtu atakayejua ni nani aliyefanya hivyo. Kwa nini akuue? Hapo watu wote wa Yuda waliokusanyika kwako wangetawanyika, na watu wachache waliobaki Yuda wangeangamizwa."

decisions.choice: a man will not know: no one will find out
decisions.reason: "A man" here means anyone at all. Johanan offers to do it secretly, so that Gedaliah would not be blamed.

decisions.choice: what was at stake: the survival of the remnant
decisions.reason: Johanan sees that Gedaliah's death would scatter the people gathered to him and destroy what was left of Judah. That is what happened: after the murder the people fled, first toward Ammon and then to Egypt (41:10-18; 43:5-7).

decisions.choice: all Judah: all the people of Judah gathered at Mizpah
decisions.reason: "Judah" here is the people, not the territory: those who had come to Gedaliah (verse 12).

decisions.choice: Nobody will find out who did it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what no one would know. It also turns the long question into a short question and a statement of the result.

decisions.choice: so that ... are scattered (Balanced); Then ... would be scattered (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the results to the question with "and". Balanced and Readable make clear that the scattering would follow from Gedaliah's death.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר גְּדַלְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָם֙ אֶל־יוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ אַֽל־תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־שֶׁ֛קֶר אַתָּ֥ה דֹבֵ֖ר אֶל־יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Gedaliah son of Ahikam to Johanan son of Kareah, Do not do the thing this, for falsehood you [are] speaking about Ishmael.

en.L: And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsehood about Ishmael."
en.B: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam answered Johanan son of Kareah, "You must not do this! What you are saying about Ishmael is false."
en.R: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam told Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this! What you are saying about Ishmael is not true."

es.L: Y Gedalías hijo de Ahicam dijo a Johanán hijo de Carea: «No hagas esto, porque hablas mentira acerca de Ismael».
es.B: Pero Gedalías hijo de Ahicam le respondió a Johanán hijo de Carea: «¡No hagas eso! Lo que dices de Ismael es falso».
es.R: Pero Gedalías hijo de Ahicam le dijo a Johanán hijo de Carea: «¡No hagas eso! Lo que dices de Ismael no es verdad».

sw.L: Lakini Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu akamwambia Yohana mwana wa Karea, "Usilitende jambo hili, kwa maana unasema uongo juu ya Ishmaeli."
sw.B: Lakini Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu akamjibu Yohana mwana wa Karea, "Usifanye jambo hili! Unayosema juu ya Ishmaeli ni uongo."
sw.R: Lakini Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu akamwambia Yohana mwana wa Karea, "Usifanye hivyo! Unayosema juu ya Ishmaeli si kweli."

decisions.choice: falsehood: Gedaliah thinks the report untrue
decisions.reason: The word means something false. Gedaliah does not necessarily accuse Johanan of lying on purpose; he refuses to believe the report. It proves true in 41:1-3, where Ishmael kills him at a meal.

decisions.choice: Do not do: the margin's form of the verb
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the scribes' marginal reading give two forms of the verb "do". The meaning is the same, and the marginal reading is followed.

decisions.choice: Gedaliah's trust
decisions.reason: Gedaliah refuses a secret killing and trusts a man of his own people. The story does not blame him outright, but the next chapter shows the cost of not heeding the warning.

decisions.choice: is false (Balanced); is not true (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the stress on the report, not on Johanan's honesty (m1).

decisions.choice: mentira (L); falso (B); no es verdad (R)
decisions.reason: *Sheqer* is "mentira" in this translation; here it is Gedaliah's mistaken charge, and Balanced and Readable soften it to "false" and "not true" as the English does.
